title: Prophet Yunus and the Whale
summary: The story of Prophet Yunus 'alaihis salam, who was swallowed by a great fish and prayed in three layers of darkness. (QS. Al-Anbiya: 87-88; QS. Ash-Shaffat: 139-148)
moral: Always repent and pray to Allah, wherever we are. Allah hears His servant's prayer and brings him out of difficulty.
pages: Prophet Yunus 'alaihis salam was sent by Allah to the people of Nineveh. He invited them to believe, but they would not listen. So he left them with an angry heart, before Allah gave permission.
He boarded a ship full of cargo. In the middle of the sea, a great storm came and waves struck the ship. After a draw, he was thrown into the sea.
By Allah's command, a great fish came and swallowed him. He was not hurt, and only Allah knew his state. At that time the great fish became the place where he prayed to Allah.

In the fish's belly, in the middle of the night and the depths of the sea, Prophet Yunus was in three layers of darkness: the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the fish's belly. He realised his mistake and humbled himself before Allah.
He prayed, 'Laa ilaaha illaa anta, subhaanaka innii kuntu minazh zhaalimiin', meaning, 'There is no god but You. Glory be to You, indeed I was among the wrongdoers.' (QS. Al-Anbiya: 87)
Allah answered his prayer and saved him from sorrow. The fish released him onto barren ground, sick. Then Allah grew a gourd plant nearby to shade him.

Prophet Yunus returned to call his people, and this time they believed. Allah accepted their faith and gave them enjoyment of life. From this story we learn to always pray and repent, for Allah is the Most Accepting of repentance. The end.
